# React Three Fiber

A React renderer for [[three-js]]: the scene graph is expressed as JSX components and reconciled like
a DOM tree. Used in [[stickfps]] at `@react-three/fiber ^9.6.1`, with `@react-three/drei ^10.7.7` for
helpers and `@react-three/postprocessing ^3.0.4` for the effect chain, on `react ^19.2.7`.

## What it buys here

**One tree for HUD and world.** Lobby, HUD, buy menu, pause menu and match-end screen are ordinary
React components sharing state with the 3D scene through the same hooks — there is no bridge between
a UI framework and a render loop, which is the usual source of duplicated state in browser games.

**`useFrame` as the render loop.** The per-frame callback is where the client's accumulator lives:
`useFixedTimestep` drains simulated steps from the frame delta, so [[fixed-timestep-simulation]] runs
inside React's loop rather than beside it.

**Escape hatches stay available.** Effects, object pools (`pooling/ObjectPool.ts`), tracers and
particles are managed imperatively where per-frame allocation would matter, and mounted declaratively
where it would not.

## Where the abstraction leaks

**React batching can eat a game event.** In [[stickfps]] the kill feed can drop an entry when two
lethal hits land inside the same React batch — two state updates collapse into one render and one of
the messages never appears. This is reported and deliberately not fixed. The general lesson: a
UI-state model tuned for "latest value wins" is the wrong shape for an **event log**, which needs
append semantics, and the bug only appears under simultaneity.

**Bundle weight.** The client ships ~1.4 MB, listed in the repo's own limitations.

**Testability splits cleanly, and that is the tell.** Client tests in [[stickfps]] cover pure
functions only — movement controller, weapon state machine, spring integrator, object pool,
reconciliation, interpolation. Anything requiring a real GL context is verified through
[[playwright]] instead. Keeping simulation logic out of components is what makes that split possible.

## Version note

The vendored R3F skill pack in the repo declares `Requires @react-three/fiber 8.x+` while the project
runs 9.6.1 — see [[agent-skills-checked-into-the-repo]] and [[documentation-drift]].
